result.summary: Stops monitoring socket exception sets in select() on non-Windows platforms, and disconnects established peers if an exception triggers on Windows. This prevents TCP urgent data or out-of-band pointers from repeatedly waking select() without readable data.
result.problem: On POSIX systems, incoming TCP urgent data triggers select()'s exception set, which can cause the network event loop to spin continuously when no regular data is available to read. Windows requires monitoring the exception set for non-blocking connect failures, but other operating systems only use it for out-of-band data.
evidence: Commit message (1fde57f1de): 'On other platforms, a TCP urgent pointer can leave the exception set pending even when no data is readable. Only monitor it on Windows, and disconnect established P2P peers if it is set.'
result.scope_notes: Alternative approach to closed PR #36688; diff was not provided in prompt data.
result.card: Stops monitoring socket exception sets in select() on non-Windows platforms and disconnects established P2P peers if an exception triggers on Windows. This fixes an issue where TCP urgent data or out-of-band pointers leave socket exceptions pending on POSIX platforms, causing network event loops to wake up repeatedly without readable data. It replaces the approach in #36688 which attempted to handle urgent data via SO_OOBINLINE.
uncertainties: Exact diff and implementation details were not provided, and quoted background text from #36688 was omitted.

risk.why: Mistakes in select() socket set handling could fail to detect connection failures or inappropriately disconnect legitimate P2P peers.
